story_text:
Picture of Pyradome Prototype I undergoing testing after successful proof of concept
## Background
Every apartment kitchen has the same quiet compromise: the smoky char you actually want is the one thing you can't get indoors. So you settle. Sheet pan instead of grate. Stovetop instead of live fire. A faint memory of what backyard flavor actually tastes like.
City living has a lot going for it. High-rises and apartment complexes put you close to everything, but they quietly take away one freedom: firing up a grill at home. Balcony rules, building policies, and a smoke alarm over every stove mean real smoke flavor gets left behind with the backyard.
That's why we started Pyradome. With our patent-pending ChimneyCore technology, we're building toward smoke-infused meals no matter where you live or what the weather is doing outside.
The design pairs a centuries-old idea with a modern one. Like a Moroccan tagine, Pyradome's dome holds heat, moisture, and aroma close around the food as it cooks. We've wrapped that timeless shape in the craftsmanship of high-end cookware: warm metals, sculpted curves, and details worth leaving out on the counter.
## Inspired by luxury. Built for real life.
## The Problem with "Indoor Smoking"
Every indoor grill on the market solves half the problem. They get you heat and grate marks, but they can't touch real wood-smoke flavor, because real smoke means real haze, real smell clinging to your curtains for a week, and a ventilation hood most kitchens simply don't have.
So the industry compromise became: give up the smoke, keep the marks. Call it good enough.
We think that's the wrong trade.
## ChimneyCore: The Patent-Pending Future of Smoke Control
Pyradome isn't an indoor grill with a fan bolted on. It's built around a single question: what if we could cook with real wood smoke and never let that smoke reach your kitchen air at all?
That's the job of ChimneyCore, our patent-pending smoke extraction system. Instead of letting smoke drift into the room and trying to clean the air afterward, ChimneyCore pulls smoke into a sealed chimney path the moment it rises off the grate and filters it before it can escape.
We've already proven the core idea works. Our proof-of-concept rig uses a small inline duct fan to draw smoke through a sealed path and two HEPA filters to capture it, and in testing it pulled and filtered smoke the way we designed it to.
Our goal for the finished appliance is simple: no haze, no smell, no exhaust hood. Just the flavor you've been missing, on any night, in any kitchen. Every prototype round is about getting closer to that, and measuring it honestly along the way.
## What We're Engineering Toward
The proof of concept validated the principle. The full appliance takes it much further, and here's the direction we're building and testing across the prototype rounds.
- A production filtration stack. The finished ChimneyCore is being designed with a more powerful fan and a multi-stage stack, including a heat-resistant, washable carbon stage you can rinse clean after cooks, and HEPA filtration to capture fine particles. We're refining the order and placement of each stage through real testing.
- Catalytic combustion. We're exploring a catalytic stage that re-burns smoke byproducts before air leaves the unit, the same category of technology used in industrial exhaust systems, scaled down for a countertop.
- Integrated sensors. Our goal is an appliance that reads the cook and manages airflow and temperature for you, so you don't have to.
- A dome built for containment. Pyradome's dome isn't just an aesthetic choice. We're building it as a working containment system: a sealed gap between an inner and outer shell, inspired by the same principle nuclear reactor containment uses, designed to keep anything that escapes the primary chamber from ever reaching open air.
- Sealed at every opening. Every access point, the fuel drawer, the water reservoir, the ash tray, is being engineered as an individually gasketed seal, using breathable high-temperature material that manages pressure without turning your countertop appliance into a pressure cooker.
- Hardware that feels intentional. A product you'll open and close every time you cook deserves hardware that feels like it. We're designing every handle, hinge, and seam on purpose: structural elements celebrated with real, visible bolted hardware; moving mechanical parts kept clean and nearly invisible.
## Where We Are Right Now
We're not asking you to fund a sketch. We've built and tested a working proof of concept of the ChimneyCore extraction system, validating that this approach actually pulls and filters smoke, and our patent applications are filed.
This campaign funds the next honest step: about ten hand-assembled working prototypes of the full appliance across build-test-revise rounds, the engineering and CAD to make the design manufacturable, and the legal and safety-certification groundwork every kitchen appliance needs before it can be sold. Each round means real testing, real fixes, and real footage of the process, not a polished reveal at the end, but the actual work of getting this right.
Platinum Founders will receive one Pyradome from our first production run. To be completely transparent: producing that first run is a separate, much larger investment, estimated at around $1.2 million, which we'll raise after this campaign. This campaign gets Pyradome to the point where that next step is possible, and we'll share every step of it with you.
## Our Vision
Some pieces earn a permanent place on the counter. The enameled pot passed down through a family. The sculptural object the whole kitchen seems to be arranged around. They're beautiful enough to leave out and made well enough to outlast every trend around them. That's where we want Pyradome to live.
Grilling has always been built for the backyard: black steel, purely utilitarian, something you hide under a cover when you're done. We think cooking with real wood smoke deserves the same care as the finest cookware, and that it belongs indoors, where people actually gather.
So the finished Pyradome is being designed as a luxury small appliance, not a gadget. Here's the design we're working toward.
## What the finished Pyradome looks like
Picture a sculpted dome about 14 inches across and 16 inches tall, roughly the footprint of a large Dutch oven, sitting on low feet on your counter. The dome is a smooth metal with a fine brushed texture that catches light softly, the kind of finish you want to run your hand across.
A band of warm brushed metal wraps the waist where the dome meets the base, punctuated by bold, visible bolts. It's structural hardware treated as jewelry. Two sculpted bronze handles curve out from each side, and a slim bronze pull sits at the front of the band so the dome lifts with one hand.
On the front of the dome is an oval viewing window framed in bronze, with its own exposed bolts, giving you a warm glimpse of the food and the smoke as it cooks. Just below it sits the Pyradome emblem: a single flame shaped into a P.
At the very top, a short bronze chimney cap crowns the dome, ringed with vent slots. That's ChimneyCore, the heart of the design, made to be seen rather than hidden.
The base carries the controls: one weighted bronze dial in the center, a smoke button to its left, and a clean red temperature readout to its right. Two finely perforated grilles flank the controls, where the unit breathes in fresh air. Everything is arranged symmetrically, quiet and deliberate, with nothing on the outside that doesn't need to be there.
Finishes, dimensions and details may evolve through prototyping, but this is the standard we're holding ourselves to: an object that looks like it belongs next to your best cookware and your finest things.
We picture it with snowfall outside, on a marble island in a city apartment, at the center of a dinner for six, doing something no other object in the room can: bringing real wood-smoke flavor to the table while the air stays clear.
## Where Pyradome goes next
ChimneyCore is the real invention, and the countertop dome is only its first home. Once the technology is proven, here's where we see it going:
- A family of sizes. A compact Pyradome for smaller kitchens and dinners for two, the signature 14-inch model, and a larger version for full gatherings and bigger cuts.
- ChimneyCore for your outdoor grill. A standalone ChimneyCore unit that mounts on a conventional grill or smoker to capture smoke at the source. Anyone who has stood over a smoky grill knows the problem: you spend the cook breathing smoke, and by the time you sit down, your senses are so full of it you can barely taste the smoke on the food. Pulling it away from the cook means less smoke in your lungs and more flavor on your plate.
- Full-size grills and smokers. Outdoor grills and smokers designed from the ground up around ChimneyCore, bringing the same containment and the same design language to the backyard.
- Cookware and accessories. Pieces made to belong with Pyradome, from grill pans and tools to smoke pods in a range of wood flavors, all held to the same standard of craft.
These are directions we're excited about, not promises attached to this campaign.
That's the destination. This campaign is the first step toward it: the working prototypes that prove the engineering underneath the design. Form will follow function, and we'll show you every step of getting there.
## Funding Milestones
Our goal covers the essential work: prototypes, engineering, and legal groundwork. Every milestone beyond it moves Pyradome closer to production.
- $50,000: About ten hand-built prototypes across three build-test-revise rounds, production CAD, and legal work.
- $75,000: Pre-certification safety testing and design-for-manufacturing refinements.
- $100,000+: A first contribution toward production, bringing the first production run closer.
## Rewards
Silver Founder ($250). The simplest way to stand behind Pyradome from day one. Your name is permanently listed as a Founder on pyradomes.com, and you'll follow every prototype round through backer-only updates.
Gold Founder ($500). For founders who want to be first in line. Everything in Silver Founder, plus your name at the top of the Founders list and a guaranteed chance to reserve your Pyradome before public reservations open.
Platinum Founder ($1000, limited to 50). One of the earliest Pyradomes ever made, at a founding price well below planned retail, shipping before any public order, plus everything in Gold Founder. Ships within the United States, with shipping calculated and charged separately before your Pyradome ships. Estimated delivery: June 2028.
## Risks and Challenges
## Hardware is hard, and we'd rather you hear the risks from us up front.
Production funding. Platinum Founder units depend on raising roughly $1.2 million for the first production run after this campaign. We're actively pursuing that funding, and our delivery estimate assumes we secure it. If it takes longer, delivery will move, and we'll tell you as soon as we know.
Design changes. Prototyping exists to find problems. The filtration stack, dimensions, and finishes may change between rounds, and we'll show you every change and why we made it.
Safety certification. Pyradome must pass electrical safety certifications before it can be sold or shipped. Testing can uncover issues that require redesign, which can add time.
Our commitment. We'll post regular updates with real footage, share what's working and what isn't, and keep communicating. If we're ever unable to deliver a reward, we'll tell you directly and follow Kickstarter's rules for making it right with backers.
## Why Back Us Now?
…(以下省略)
risks: Pyradome combines real engineering complexity, indoor smoke filtration, catalytic combustion, sealed containment, with the genuine unpredictability of iterative hardware prototyping. Here's what we're watching, and how we're de-risking it. Engineering risk. ChimneyCore isn't a single novel invention, it's a deliberate combination of proven technologies: HEPA and activated carbon fiber filtration, catalytic combustion, and sensor-based automation. We're validating the full stack through hands-on prototype testing rather than asking backers to fund an unproven concept on paper. Iteration risk. Hardware prototyping is a build-test-revise process, not a straight line. Our plan accounts for roughly three rounds, each with real testing and real fixes between them, and our funding goal includes buffer specifically for the unpredictable parts of that process, tooling rework, material changes, unexpected fixes. We'll communicate openly through every round so you're never wondering where things stand.

faq.q: Does Pyradome really eliminate smoke, or just reduce it?
faq.a: Pyradome is engineered to dramatically reduce smoke and odor escaping into your kitchen through ChimneyCore's multi-stage filtration (mesh, HEPA, activated carbon) plus catalytic combustion that re-burns smoke byproducts before exhaust exits the unit. We're actively testing this system now. No indoor cooking appliance can promise literally zero smell with any food, ever, but our goal is a night-and-day difference from cooking with an open flame indoors.

faq.q: Can I still get real wood-smoke flavor if the smoke is being filtered out?
faq.a: Yes, filtration happens after the smoke has already done its job flavoring your food. ChimneyCore captures and neutralizes smoke on its way out of the chamber, not before it contacts what you're cooking.

faq.q: Does it use real wood or charcoal, or just electric heat?
faq.a: Pyradome uses an electrical heating system and real wood pellets for smoke, not liquid smoke or flavor additives, combined with temperature control for consistency.
We're still finalizing final production specs, but the extraction fan is sized for continuous kitchen use, similar in profile to a range hood on a low setting, not a shop vac.

faq.q: What's the dishwasher-safe part, and what isn't?
faq.a: The interior dome liner and cooking surface are designed to be removable and dishwasher-safe for easy cleanup. The outer shell, base, and other hardware are wipe-clean, not dishwasher-safe, the same way you'd care for any other countertop appliance with electrical components.

faq.q: How often do I need to replace the filter?
faq.a: We're determining exact replacement intervals through testing, but the ChimneyCore cartridge is designed as a swappable part, not a whole-unit replacement, and will be available through our spare parts store.

faq.q: What happens to the ash and spent pellets?
faq.a: Pyradome plans to include a dedicated proprietary ash and pellet system for easy clean-out between uses.
